capabilities.description: Render details and module-specific actions for the currently selected real module in the collapsible module tree.
Provide the full canonical identifier of each displayed module independently of its short name and directory.
uncertainties: The current detail header displays the module name and directory, but not the canonical identifier as a distinct selectable value.

capabilities.description: Let a keyboard or pointer user copy the selected real module's exact canonical identifier from its module-tree detail panel without changing tree interaction state.
uncertainties: No clipboard-writing behavior was found in the bounded architect-view searches; this is not proof that no unrelated clipboard helper exists outside the inspected candidates.
Exact control placement and wording can be resolved during local engineering and do not block identifying the owning capability.

capabilities.description: Announce copy success or failure for the module whose request completed, retain a selectable manual-copy value on failure, and suppress stale outcomes after selection changes.
uncertainties: The retained view contains no existing clipboard outcome behavior to reuse.
The exact accessible announcement text and visual duration can be resolved during local engineering; neither blocks the bounded consumer capability.

relationships.reason: The copy action appears only in the detail panel for a selected real module.
The copied text is the selected displayed module's canonical identifier rather than its name or directory.
Feedback reflects the asynchronous outcome of the copy request and remains associated with the identifier captured when that request began.
Feedback is rendered only with the matching selected module detail and is absent for the project summary or no selection.

seams.agreementNeeded: The action is present only when the detail represents a real selected module, and activation does not invoke selection, collapse, open-module, refresh, or graph-position behavior.
The clipboard payload and manual-copy value are exactly the displayed module's id with no label, transformation, or added whitespace.
Each pending result retains the initiating module id; success or failure is announced only while that same module remains selected, and failure keeps that id visible and selectable.

openQuestions: Non-blocking for the initial bounded consumer goal: choose concise success and failure wording and the lifetime of transient success feedback during local engineering.

Non-blocking for the initial bounded consumer goal: decide whether the canonical identifier is always shown as selectable text or whether an additional manual-copy presentation appears only after failure, while preserving the requirement that failure leaves it visible and selectable.
Non-blocking for the initial bounded consumer goal: define the local fallback behavior for a missing clipboard API and rejected clipboard promises without introducing fresh analysis or server work.
